definitions.explanation: Describes something that catches one's interest because it is rare or unfamiliar. Often implies looking at something with wide-eyed curiosity, as if encountering it for the first time.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧たち⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{物珍|ものめずら}しそう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{見|み}ていた→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: The children were watching with curiosity.

examples.japanese: ⟦{外国|がいこく}→外国：02868_gaikoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{食|た}べ{物|もの}→食べ物：02890_tabemono⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{物珍|ものめずら}しくて⟦{色々|いろいろ}→色々：02352_iroiro⟧⟦{試|ため}した→試す：02130_tamesu⟧。
examples.english: I was curious about foreign foods and tried all sorts of things.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最初|さいしょ}→最初：00882_saisho⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{物珍|ものめずら}しかった⟦{田舎|いなか}→田舎：01320_inaka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦すっかり→すっかり：01270_sukkari⟧⟦{慣|な}れた→慣れる：00870_nareru⟧。
examples.english: I've gotten completely used to rural life, which at first seemed so novel.

notes:
USAGE:
{物珍|ものめずら}しい often appears in the adverbial form {物珍|ものめずら}しそう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ ("as if finding something novel") to describe the way someone looks at or reacts to something unfamiliar. The nuance is lighter than ⟦{珍|めずら}しい→珍しい：01200_mezurashii⟧ alone, emphasizing the curiosity of the observer.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {物珍|ものめずら}しそう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧ (to look at with curiosity)
- {物珍|ものめずら}しさ (novelty, unfamiliarity)
- {物珍|ものめずら}しい⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧ (to look at with curious eyes)

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦{珍|めずら}しい→珍しい：01200_mezurashii⟧ is the more common and general word for "rare" or "unusual." {物珍|ものめずら}しい specifically emphasizes the viewer's sense of novelty and curiosity.
